issues.body: Section 7 says `worker_min_samples` should gate on the count of attributed no-change rows rather than `worker_attempts_1h`. For `worker_no_change_rate_1h = attributed_no_change / worker_attempts`, the attempts are the observations and therefore the sample size. The proposed guard instead counts only positive outcomes, making alert eligibility outcome-dependent: e.g. 100 attributable attempts with 2 no-change outcomes is a 100-run sample but would be treated as only two samples. Attribution quality is a separate completeness property and cannot be represented by counting only joined no-change rows. The surrounding recommendation also calls the prospective high-bad threshold `worker_no_change_floor`; a no-change alert should fire above a ceiling, not below a floor, unless a different predicate is explicitly defined.
issues.fix_hint: Keep the minimum-sample guard on the rate denominator (`worker_attempts_1h`). Track attribution completeness separately (for example, an always-emitted unattributed count and/or coverage ratio), and defer/refuse alert evaluation when attribution is not sufficiently trustworthy. Specify a high-side threshold with consistent naming such as `worker_no_change_ceiling`, including its exact predicate and boundary behavior.
issues.title: Alert sample guard counts outcomes instead of observations

verdict.summary: The record usefully identifies the missing repository dimension and several publication/retention seams, but its recommended alert design contains a material statistical error. It proposes using the number of attributed no-change rows as the minimum-sample guard for a rate whose denominator is worker attempts. That counts positive outcomes rather than observations and makes the alert's eligibility depend on the outcome being detected. The threshold direction/name is also left inconsistent: no-change is bad when high, whereas a `floor` convention describes a low-side trigger. This needs correction before the document is safe to use as the implementation design.
